cues.en: All right.
In this section we are going to look at tree data structure.
Now what is a tree data structure.
By definition a tree is a non-linear data structure with hierarchical relationship between its elements
without having any cycle.
It's basically a reversed form of real life tree.
So what does it mean?
So let's look at this in real life example.
And you will notice that we are using tree data structures in our daily life.
Let's say we are in cafe and we want to order a drink.
So when we want to order the drink we have two options.
We can order either hot drinks or cold drinks.
So this means that for drinks we have two branches.
Now again within these options we have multiple sub options.
So if we want to order hot drinks we have two options.
We can order tea or coffee.
Similarly if we want to order the cold drinks we have also two options.
Over here we can order alcoholic drinks or non-alcoholic drinks.
So if you go one step further, we can see that in case of tea, we have black tea and green tea.
In case of coffee we have three types of coffee over here Americano, latte or cappuccino.
Now when it comes to the cold drinks, if we go for non-alcoholic drinks, we can see that we have three
options over here Cola, Fanta and soda.
And for alcoholic drinks, we have wine and beer.
So we see that drinks in cafes menu have been ordered in a nice hierarchy, which makes it easier for
customers to choose.
They might not be aware that they are using a tree data structure, but this way of organizing the data
in the cafe menu makes it easier for customers and owners as well.
Now, in the world of data structure, this structure is called tree data structure.
As you see, without being aware of, we are using a tree data structure in our daily lives.
So the diagram that we see over here represents a typical tree data structure structures in computer
science.
Now let's see what are the common properties and observations from this diagram.
So I'm just going to make it a little bit smaller.
So the first property in this diagram is it is used to represent data in hierarchical form.
It means that every time when we go one step further it becomes more specialized form of its parent.
So here we have the links.
Then if you go one step forward we see that we can select hot and cold drinks.
So this means that this is more specialized way of the drink.
Then if you go further we see that we have coffee and tea and it continues like this.
So this means that every time we go one step further we are doing specialization.
In other words, we are maintaining a hierarchical form.
Now let's continue to the next property which is every node has two components that is data and reference
to its subcategory.
If we look at the drink node over here, we see that it has the data which is drink and it has the reference
to the subcategory.
So in this case we have a reference to the hot and we have a reference to the cold.
So this node over here holds in it data.
And the reference to it is sub category, which means that it also stores the address of the sub categories.
In this case it stores the address of the hot and cold drinks.
So as you remember, in case of linked list in the node, we were having the value and next reference
to the node.
So here again is applicable.
We are having the address of the sub categories and the data which is the value.
Now the next property of this diagram is at the top we have a base category.
Then we have sub categories under this base category.
In case of typical tree we have as many as sub categories under one category.
There is no limit for sub categories in this case.
So these are the properties that can be driven from this diagram.
Now let's see the tree data structure.
And it's not a surprise that we have the same properties for the tree data structure.
Now this is a typical representation of the tree data structure.
So here we have n one as a root and it has the subsequent nodes.
So if we closely examine this tree, we can see that it represents a hierarchical order.
So at the top we have n one.
Then we have n two and three.
Then it continues like this.
So the first property is satisfied.
Then we can easily see that every node has two components.
The first component is the data and the second component is the references to its subcategories.
So in this case for n one we have a references to n two and three.
And for n two we have references to n four and five.
And from n three we have a reference to n six.
Now we continue to the last property, we can easily see that n one is the top node, which is a root
node, and it is the first node in the tree.
Then it has subsequent nodes under it which is n2 and n3, and it continues like this.
So this means that the third property also is satisfied.
So these are the main properties of tree data structure.
And hopefully everything is clear about what is a tree data structure.
Now in the next lecture let's look at where do we need a tree data structure.
